rv.q: The result is harrowing but also deeply humane, a piece of theater whose darkness makes its flashes of beauty all the more affecting.
It is evocative, satisfying, and memorable theater.
The House of the Negro Insane is that most devilish thing, a play that is just good enough to make one wish it was so very much better.
The acting is convincing, not as solo performances but as an ensemble inhabiting the same social rules and emotional reality of the asylum.

cn.t: Anthony's searing drama about a Jim Crow-era psychiatric institution proves evocative and memorable despite flaws, with critics praising its powerful excavation of racist history and strong performances.
